reviews.text: rostrain 2 takes everything that worked in the first game and makes it even better. The atmosphere is darker, the survival mechanics are more refined, and the overall experience feels deeper and more polished. It respects what made the original special while confidently pushing the series forward. If you enjoyed the first game, this sequel is not just more of the same, it’s the best version of it. [b]Honestly, at this point buying Frostrain 2 should probably be considered basic human responsibility.[/b]

玩了二十几个小时之后的一点碎碎念： 学院线很轮椅，集齐4羁绊就可以自己产生组件，不知道玩啥就玩学院。商人线也相当不错，会给很多道具。当然，推荐大家什么线都可以玩一玩。 崔顺子：普通和难度1都是随便打，难度2开始最好走右线，无人机选项-1对走什么线都挺伤的 林锡大：军队线，宗教线，民主线都可以走，不过军队线数值更强，宗教线个人觉得其实一般，民主线可以点决策最快攒出学院羁绊。就是要注意，如果不是想走紧张度线，难度3最好一开始先点胡萝卜和大棒消紧张度，不然紧张度随随便便就爆了 乔米米公测的内容很有意思，总体上和崔顺子很像，除了发放补给和列车提速两个保命国策之外，一条探索+承诺线，一条军政财线。以防你不知道军政财线点完国策可以用统治行为实现电表倒转（详细可以看我B站上的视频BV1o9N76oE5R） 希望制作组以后可以加入创意工坊，加入创意工坊之后肯定会更好玩

游戏的事件很多（虽然有些是固定事件会重复），每个人的地图是固定的但各不相同，流派很多，因此前5-8小时趣味性还是很高的，但缺点是目前不是很平衡——没错说的就是你学院流。游戏内一没有提升流派权重的机制，刷卡牌/车厢看脸，二是很缺物资，升级和买卡牌/车厢要大量物资（尤其是后期升级要大量物资，以及后期车厢升级也要花物资刷出对应的大量卡牌）。而我们的学院流呢？两个学院车厢就能40s给一张学院卡，四个学院车厢就能10s给一张学院卡，学院车厢还能升5级，其它流派最高只有4级，简直是轮椅中的轮椅。希望之后能平衡一下数值，最起码加强一下其它流派或出个提高流派权重的机制，不然除学院外的流派看起来很有意思，玩起来却有些脑溢血，到后期花光物资也全是2、3级的小卡拉米。
体感上有卡组检测。 棱彩卡就那几张，应该是四张，我就差一张，但是我九级，二十多个补给下去，其他三张棱彩一直来，唯独看不到我想要的。黄金卡也是，后期缺的时候，非常难抽到，其他流派的黄金卡一直来，怎么都抽不到你想要的。 以上不是一个档这样。
游戏还可以，但我玩这游戏老崩溃，三小时崩三次了，有什么办法吗

《霜轨：Frostrain 2》作为续作全方位升级，是融合卡牌构筑、生存经营的顶尖肉鸽佳作，Steam 收获特别好评，极简黑白雪景美术完美烘托冰封末日的孤寂压迫感，沉浸感无可替代。游戏跳出传统生存套路，以列车车厢卡牌为核心构筑体系，数百种神器遗物搭配海量车厢联动，流派搭配自由度极高，每一局随机地图、事件、补给都带来全新体验，重玩价值拉满。 玩家化身末代列车长，既要规划雪原行进路线、搜集物资抵御暴雪与极端天灾，还要平衡乘客幸福度、维持车内秩序，一旦民心崩溃便会触发叛乱，资源分配与人性抉择双线施压，全程充满紧绷的策略紧迫感游侠网。六边形地标探索、随机史诗事件、商店构筑机制丰富玩法深度，新增多角色列车长解锁体系，通关积累货币解锁永久遗物，长线养成顺滑不肝。 没有冗余复杂操作，资源循环逻辑严谨，音效贴合雪原寒风氛围，完整简体中文适配新手。不管是喜欢卡牌协同构筑、末日生存模拟，还是偏爱多结局肉鸽闯关的策略玩家，这款兼具氛围感与深度的独立策略游戏都值得反复钻研，每一次驶向终点的旅途都独一无二。
还算有趣的数值经营游戏。 好消息是可以凑羁绊，肉鸽道具池有点深度，可以构思多种不同的通关解法。 坏消息是游戏通关的核心机制只有单一数值，每个角色的故事路线固定，随机事件不够丰富，构思再多build也难以在匮乏的通关玩法上玩出花来，重复游玩性并不算高。

It's fun (and to some extent intense), but it does need some adjustments in my opinion. (Mild spoilers ahead). The biggest flaw in this game, in my opinion, is that at the base difficulty you really only will lose right at the end, and it'll be a very unsatisfying loss that is essentially failing at a DPS check. To elaborate, unless you're doing *really* well, it's not particularly transparent whether you'll make it through the end, whether that be the poison cloud, the brothers at the end, etc., and it's way worse at difficulty three. You can show up near the end with around 30k happiness banked up and 130+ speed and still barely not make it. This is more an issue for Choi Soonja than for Im Seokdae since Seokdae has the one branch that dramatically buffs late game happiness. But like it's a smidge unsatisfying when you get a full Ivory Tower setup by midgame and still lose just before the end because you didn't get enough relics that directly buff happiness. Successfully completing the build for any of the major paths by midgame should give you enough time to prepare for the endgame. The way in which you add difficulty also needs adjustment, especially for Soonja. Making the unhappiness scale stupidly fast is not an exciting way to add challenge, in part because it dramatically restricts which strategies are feasible. For example, there are tons of artifacts that try to get you to interact with the blizzard, but in my experience at difficulty 3 if you're even seeing the blizzard you're probably not going fast enough to beat the ridiculous amounts of unhappiness at the end - even if you have speed 130+. Seokdae's difficulty 1 adding speed to the blizzard is a great idea since it forces you to interact with MORE of the game. It might be more work, but I think ideally you'd also have a few events that are unique to higher difficulties as well, since that might make the challenge more interesting than a DPS check at the end. Some ideas for other ways to adjust difficulty are: - Overcrowding penalty increases to 2%/passenger; - Certain marked nodes temporarily hurt move speed; - More poison clouds scattered throughout the map; - Hand size is constrained; - Cycle length increases by 50% (multiplying through by any cycle length adjustments you may have). - Each level requires more exp to achieve. Notice that each of these demand that you interact with more aspects of the game, for example artifacts affecting contamination become more viable when there are more poison clouds, and artifacts affecting the blizzard become more viable when your train speed is reduced. Another change I'd recommend, seconding what others here have said, is that you need to change the supply system a smidge since otherwise it's tedious if you collect too many (for example if you're going a transportation strategy midgame). I'd recommend you either make supplies useful for more things or scrap them and go back to "receive a drone" rather than a currency. To elaborate, other than Joe Mimi's ability to spend supply to increase economic stability, no activities require you to have supply sitting around ready for use. Some artifacts benefit from having supply available, but no events directly interact with it but rather give you supply shortages. I feel like there should be events that could happen where an option says something like "Pay 10 supply" and it's locked unless you actually have 10 supply. This is more impactful than supply shortages, since it means you actively need to have supply available or else you might need to take a less favorable route. Another simpler route is adding the ability to purchase more expensive things with supplies (for example, 10 supplies for an artifact, or a variance reduction thing like "Spend 3 extra supplies to guarantee your choices include a red"). The choice between exp or train is a smidge boring, since after early game it's usually very obvious which you want. Another person mentioned that the identity of each individual card doesn't really matter, and I strongly agree with that; in Frostrain 1 (which I played after this), you did have to actually look at what the text on the card says. In this game, after one round you essentially could know exactly what the card does just by looking at the picture. I think having a platinum tier cards actually have special abilities like in the first game would add more depth, since otherwise the only way to boost beyond the synergies in through artifacts, but without dramatically rehauling your train to go religion you cannot use supplies to interact with artifacts and so you'd pretty much be out of luck. For example, if you're going with an academy build, getting a train with 8 tier five buildings isn't enough for Soonja difficulty 3 without additionally a swarm artifacts. But there's little-to-no incentive to branch out to other directions still besides the religion direction, since the cycle-time benefit and the train-speed benefits won't suffice. Lastly a few quality of life things are needed. To be honest, I pretty much only ever play at 10x speed or paused, since it seems there's nothing that happens that requires you to not be at 10x speed, but this means that if I don't have high sight I sometimes am a bit late to click on the next turn. Idk how the game decides which way to move you, but a solid fraction of the time it will literally move you directly towards the blizzard, and that half a second lapse is often enough to end the 30 minute run. This is stupid - if you don't select a direction, should default to move east, and then randomly amongst east-facing options, or something like that. I lost one time because the train defaulted to turn left directly in front of the tree at the very end, and I hadn't selected the direction because the limit of my vision when I had clicked it a few seconds earlier was right in front of the tree. Also, clicking a path should send you towards that path - it seems currently it's clicking nodes sends you towards a node, but that's a smidge counterintuitive to me and perhaps both options should be available. Also, there needs to be an "auto-merge hand" and "auto-sort hand" option, since otherwise academy builds are a mess merging all the ivory towers. Overall, I'd say it's a good game, and certainly if you go a purple-train or yellow-train strategy you can get the "break the game" feeling that you get with roguelike deckbuilders, but some more polishing is necessary before it's perfect.

I heard the game had finally left Early Access, so I figured it was time to leave a review. A friend recommended it to me, and I’ve been playing since Early Access. It’s genuinely a lot of fun. Every run requires you to constantly adapt your synergies and plan or revise your route based on the cards and artifacts you pick up along the way. Finding a way to make everything work and successfully complete a run is incredibly satisfying. The concept of a train racing through a snowy landscape is also incredibly charming. It’s been a long time since a game made me completely lose track of time like this. I haven’t had a chance to try Mimi yet because I’ve been busy with work, but I’m really looking forward to playing her soon!
